newsitem.title: USA: Enron comfortable with EPS estimates.
newsitem.headline: Enron comfortable with EPS estimates.

text.p: Enron Corp executives on Wednesday said the company is targeting first quarter earnings in the range of analysts' $0.85-$0.91 a share estimates, and expects to post earnings in the "upper end" of $2.40-$2.60 a share earnings forecast for the year.
Enron Chairman Ken Lay said the company remains on track to post cumulative 15 percent a share earnings growth through the end of the decade.
The company on Jan. 21 posted $2.31 a share earnings for 1996, up 12 percent on the year but raised concerns among analysts that the company fell short of its earnings target.
"We still expect to have cumulative growth in earnings per share within the five-year period of 15 percent per year, which would basically double our earnings per share during that period," Lay said.
The company last year announced the target of doubling primary earnings to $4 a share by the year 2000.
Enron still expects to post annual double-digit earnings growth, with accelerating growth in earnings over the next three years from increased international and domestic revenues.

"If anything, some of our new business areas appear to be growing faster and unfolding faster than we even expected a year ago," he said, referring to the company's domestic wholesale electricity and international power businesses.

Enron's electricity trading arm has booked 30 million megawatt hours in the first quarter and is on pace to rack up $4 billion in electric sales this year, up from 60 million megawatt hours and $1.1 billion sales in the full year 1996.
